name_note: GTDB places this species as s__Tidjanibacter inops (representative genome from NCBI organism Tidjanibacter massiliensis), while the overwhelming majority of genomes and the literature use the name Alistipes inops.

sentences.text: Alistipes inops is an obligately anaerobic, non-spore-forming, rod-shaped, non-motile, Gram-negative bacterium described from human faeces.
The describing strain of Alistipes inops was reported as fastidious and slow-growing, indole-positive, with a non-fermentative metabolism producing acetic and succinic acids.
A review lists Alistipes inops among Alistipes species typically isolated from the human gut microbiome, a genus whose members have also been recovered from clinical samples.
The same review describes contrasting evidence for the genus Alistipes, with reported protective effects in some diseases and reported associations with colorectal cancer and depression.
